judgements.justification: B's critics (69AE from variational inference, ATkA from information bottleneck) objected to Definition 1's framing, not the technical results; A's 9TAc found it 'very difficult to digest' and moved on, and B's AC counted the framing against the paper.

B lacked a champion, but its most positive reviewers included ATkA, who studied the paper closely and argued against 69AE ('In contrast to reviewer 69AE'); the light, disengaged top reviewer the reason names is absent.
B's AC rejected because the promised rewrite was 'a major revision' needing resubmission, while A's AC took the same scope fixes (extension to g, narrower claims) as camera-ready changes.
B's meta-review rests on the visible reviews (69AE's VAE objection, ATkA's scope critique); no off-record assessment appears.
Both committees judged the paper as theory; they priced the same overclaiming differently (R06) rather than applying a contribution-type standard only one held.
69AE's held 5 rested on applicability to VAEs, which is central to the paper's claims, not a peripheral point.
